quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: You must use your low beams when:
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water and create glare, making it harder to see. Many vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left at a green light to yield to oncoming traffic. You can complete your turn when it is safe.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your car before backing. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to see through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: You are stopped behind other vehicles at a stop sign. After the vehicles ahead pass through with no cross traffic, you:

options.text: May go through the intersection without stopping again.
Must stop at the stop sign or stop line before going.
May slowly roll past the stop sign.
May follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop at the stop sign or stop line before going.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before going. Do not skip this step even if other cars are moving.

questions.question: You are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and lights on. You should:

options.text: Stop right away in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Finish going through the intersection, then pull right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish going through the intersection, then pull right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle with lights and/or siren approaches, finish crossing. Then drive to the right and stop. Always yield to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using lights or sirens.

questions.question: On long trips, you can avoid getting drowsy by:

options.text: Moving your eyes from side to side while driving.

questions.explanation: To avoid drowsiness on long drives, stop regularly to rest and stretch. Do this even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: At night, you may use parking lights instead of headlights.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive at night with only parking lights. You must use headlights when it is dark or visibility is poor.

questions.question: You cannot safely pass on a two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can see the road clearly ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming cars.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.

questions.explanation: Safe passing requires that you can see ahead clearly, you can get back to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your car is fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near their backs that you cannot see in side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water sits on the road. At speeds up to 35 mph, most tires push water away. Above 35 mph, tires cannot clear water as well and may lose grip, making your car slide like water skis.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A highway entrance ramp is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
Speed up to keep your right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When safe, you should make room for vehicles merging into your lane.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slowing down gives the other driver enough space to complete their pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: Vehicles behind a school bus with red flashing lights must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm goes up and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm goes up and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: You must stay stopped until the red lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled in, and the bus moves again.

questions.question: When crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto the tracks, check that you have enough room to cross completely. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing.

questions.question: Why should you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane?
questions.explanation: A white cane means the person is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: A police officer tells you to go through a red light. What should you do?

options.text: Wait for the light to turn green.
Come to a complete stop first.

questions.explanation: Police officer directions always override traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's instructions.

questions.question: Only ____ reduces blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol from your system. Nothing else, like eating or drinking, can speed this up.

questions.question: At an intersection with stop signs on all corners, yield to any driver:
questions.explanation: Vehicles go through a four-way stop in the order they arrive. If cars arrive at the same time, the one on the right goes first.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, worsens your vision, distorts your judgment of speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take risks. It does not help you calm down or concentrate.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Does not increase the chance of a crash.
Increases your ability to react to a hazard.

questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to dangerous driving decisions.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. Turning right here is unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: If you come to an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Wait for the green light before proceeding.
Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Watch for crossing traffic and pedestrians before you proceed.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks are permitted on an upcoming narrow bridge.
The bridge ahead is open to one-way traffic only.
The bridge ahead is wide enough for only one car at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that the upcoming bridge is narrow. You may not be able to safely meet or pass a truck on this bridge. Drive carefully.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to lose traction because of water on the road, you should:

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.
Apply the brakes firmly to prevent your vehicle from sliding.
Slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: When driving in heavy rain, your tires can lose contact with the road and ride on a layer of water. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not brake.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is not true?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
It is best to use snow tires on your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter is difficult and requires extra care. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: In rainy weather, be most careful when turning or stopping:

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars mixes with rain during this time, making roads very slippery.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and check for oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.
When passing, wait until you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.explanation: Always signal at least 100 feet before passing. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots. Wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: Drivers making a left turn must yield to all vehicles coming from the opposite direction. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at collisions or unusual events:

options.text: Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.

questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at collisions or other unusual events. This practice, called rubbernecking, causes traffic congestion and delays.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that the road may be slippery when wet. Drive carefully in wet conditions.

questions.question: True or False: When driving in fog, you should use your high beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams bounce off the fog and reflect back toward you, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs slow your nervous system. They reduce alertness, lower concentration, slow reaction time, and damage coordination. All of these are critical to safe driving.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the curb.

questions.question: What must you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. On one-way streets, move toward the nearest road edge.
